notes: Scan 015 is autograph page 5, with a separate pale pencil foliation 14 at lower left. The page is upright and has no date. It begins with impliquent as a continuation; no other page was consulted.

The page writes the epimorphism assertions b′ for binary products and c′ for a fibre product, then states a single finite-diagram hypothesis under a circled Hyp heading. It gives a canonical inverse-limit comparison and a parenthetical restriction to objects in A and three displayed indexing shapes. The final question asks whether the condition can hold without phi_! being left exact. This is a description of the written argument, not a proof check.

The original page and exactly two native-resolution halves were viewed. The original half boxes were [0,0,1686,1296] and [0,1061,1686,2357], overlapping by 235 pixels, approximately ten percent of page height. No rotation was needed. Nine first-pass crops were made and viewed; their original coordinates are recorded in crop_boxes.

At scan 015, upper formulas, all three occurrences of phi_! in b′ and all four in c′ were read with the visible exclamation-mark subscript. In c′ the F base on the source fibre product and phi_!(F) base on the target product are retained. The G/H-to-F diagram has exactly three objects and two arrows, both ending at F.

At scan 015, central display, both limit symbols carry left-pointing arrows beneath lim and index I. The comparison arrow points right. The broken-looking right parenthesis after the left F_i is retained as a parenthesis; the local paper fold/faintness does not introduce a different symbol.

Both supplied C doubts are resolved from their viewed crops: unique in the transition paragraph and 2 in the last Hyp 2′ reference. Each resolution is logged with differs_C=true even though it confirms C’s first reading.

At scan 015, parenthetical examples, the discrete shapes contain respectively one filled point and two unconnected filled points. The third shape has two upper filled points, one lower filled point and two arrows directed to the lower point. Their topology and filled-point state are retained; no arrows join the two upper points.

At scan 015, final three lines, the source gives the written abbreviation ex.t followed by an accented à, and gauche ? on the next line. H expands the abbreviation, reads the accented à as a question mark and reads gauche as Quand. C’s ending is retained. The written equals sign standing in the phrase soit = is retained literally.

No deletion, insertion, overwritten replacement or marginal verbal addition was found. The oval around Hyp is an enclosure, not a cancellation. The arrow strokes under the limit signs belong to the limit notation, not to underlining or deletion.

H’s introductory Page 5 note and its following section heading/editorial note are not source text. The source has no ellipsis before impliquent. All 24 supplied differences rows are explicitly covered, separating genuine readings from TeX syntax and alignment artifacts.

Line count 21 comprises 19 main physical writing/formula rows plus the autograph 5 and pencil 14. The circled Hyp is on the same row as Pour tout diagramme fini, and compact diagram object levels are inventoried separately rather than counted as additional running rows.

The first reader performed no mathematical proof reasoning. The main reader subsequently checked the singleton-index comparison as recorded below; the page’s general equivalence and final question remain unchecked.

The circled Hyp is an enclosed textual heading. It is represented by the standard textcircled command, with no TikZ rendering of the word. This preserves the reading and enclosure and is not counted as a change against C.

Main-reader check at the parenthetical indexing shapes (p05): the first shape is one filled point, not an empty-set sign. For a category consisting of one object and its identity only, the limit of a diagram is its sole object, so the canonical comparison under any functor is the identity. Thus this displayed singleton case imposes no nontrivial terminal-object condition. Its stated correspondence to Hyp 1 is anomalous under that interpretation; an empty indexing diagram would instead test the terminal object, but no empty diagram is substituted for the ink.

Independent audit: all seven differing encodings retain the same ink reading. The enclosure around the whole word Hyp is encoded as an inline TikZ oval with a text node so the three letters fit inside it; this replaces the single-character textcircled implementation without changing enclosure scope or correction counts. The final question retains the written equals abbreviation and the visible t after ex. The blind reader noted the central hypothesis/limit block outside the boxes; root checked the stipulated box criteria: it contains no handwritten numeral, doubt, alteration, marginal text, witness-word disagreement, or lower-confidence departure requiring an additional second-reading box.
